shortDescription: A remote border waterfall in Naikhongchhari, also called the Golden Waterfall for its sunlit rock glow.
overview: Chakdhala Waterfall sits in Naikhongchhari Upazila of Bandarban District, only about 3–4 km from the Myanmar border. Locals often call it Chakdhala Border Waterfall. When sunlight hits the mineral-rich rocks behind the falling water, the cliffs can glow with a golden tone — that is why many travelers also know it as the Golden Waterfall.

For nature lovers it is still a fresh destination: clear hill streams, quiet green surroundings, and a trek that feels far from busy tourist beaches. The path passes village tracks, bamboo bridges, and short uphill–downhill stretches before you reach the falls.

Expect roughly 1.5 hours of trekking each way depending on pace and weather. Because this is a remote border-adjacent area, travel with a local guide, start early, and follow current security advice before you go.

whatToSee.title: Main waterfall
whatToSee.description: The main cascade dropping over rocky slopes into a natural pool — the core reason to make this trek.

whatToSee.title: Stream path (jhiripath)
whatToSee.description: Cold clear water flowing beside the trail; a refreshing break point on the way up and down.

whatToSee.title: Hill trails
whatToSee.description: Village paths, bamboo bridges, and forested slopes that make the journey part of the experience.

whatToSee.title: Hill village life
whatToSee.description: Quiet rural settlements on the approach route — greet locals respectfully and ask before taking photos.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take an AC or non-AC bus to Cox's Bazar (about 9–11 hours) or to Chittagong first, then continue to Cox's Bazar / Ramu.
From Cox's Bazar or Ramu, hire a CNG, reserved microbus, or bike toward Naikhongchhari Bazar (roughly 1.5–2.5 hours depending on traffic and stops).
From Naikhongchhari Bazar, continue by local CNG/bike toward Chakdhala Bazar / the trailhead (about 30–45 minutes).
From the trailhead, trek about 1–1.5 hours through village paths, bamboo bridges, and hill trails to reach Chakdhala Waterfall. Hire a local guide at the bazar if you do not know the route.
whereToStay: There is usually no proper hotel right beside the waterfall. Most travelers stay in Cox's Bazar (wide hotel range) or, if available, simpler lodges around Naikhongchhari. For multi-day Bandarban trips, you can also base in Bandarban Sadar and day-trip with an early start. Always confirm the latest road and permit situation before booking remote stays.
whereToEat: Eat a full meal at Naikhongchhari Bazar or Cox's Bazar before starting the trek. Near the waterfall itself there are typically no reliable restaurants or shops, so do not depend on buying food on the trail.
foodToCarry: Drinking water (at least 1–2 liters per person)
tips: Start early morning so you can return before dark.
Wear shoes with good grip — rocks and bamboo bridges can be slippery.
Carry cash; mobile banking points may be limited near the trail.
Do not litter; pack all trash back to the bazar.
Check local news / guide advice about border-area access on your travel date.
safety: This is a remote hill and border-adjacent route. Trek with a local guide, avoid night travel on the trail, and follow any instructions from local administration or security checkpoints.

shortDescription: The Daughter of the Sea — rare Bangladesh beach for both sunrise and sunset over the Bay of Bengal.
overview: Kuakata in Patuakhali is famous as the Daughter of the Sea. From one shoreline you can watch sunrise and sunset over the Bay of Bengal — a rare combination in Bangladesh and the main reason travelers come here.

The beach is quieter than Cox's Bazar, with soft sand, fishing boats, and nearby Rakhine cultural stops. A weekend trip from Dhaka by launch or bus is enough for sunrise, sunset, and a calm coastal break.
Budget carefully for transport and hotel; seafood and optional mangrove boat trips are usually extra.

whatToSee.title: Sunrise & sunset beach
whatToSee.description: Stand on the same shore for both golden hours — Kuakata's signature experience.

whatToSee.title: Gangamati Reserved Forest
whatToSee.description: Seasonal mangrove views and short boat options near the coast.

whatToSee.title: Rakhine community & temple
whatToSee.description: Learn about local Rakhine culture and visit nearby Buddhist sites respectfully.

whatToSee.title: Lebur Char / nearby chars
whatToSee.description: Tide-dependent char visits for open bay landscapes.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a direct bus to Kuakata (about 10–12 hours) or an overnight launch toward Barisal, then bus to Kuakata (about 3–4 hours).
AC bus tickets Dhaka–Kuakata commonly cost around ৳1,000–৳1,600 one way depending on operator and season.
Inside Kuakata, use CNG/auto for short hops between hotel, beach points, and market (৳100–৳400 typical short rides).
For Gangamati or char trips, hire a local boat only after checking tide and weather the same morning.
whereToStay: Sea-facing hotels and budget lodges line the Kuakata beach road. Budget rooms often start near ৳1,500–৳2,500 per night; cleaner mid-range sea-view hotels commonly run ৳3,000–৳6,000. Book ahead on weekends and peak winter dates.
whereToEat: Beach-road restaurants serve rice meals, grilled fish, and shutki dishes. Have heavier meals in town; for early sunrise, keep snacks in your room.
tips: Winter mornings give the clearest sunrise.
Negotiate CNG fares before boarding.
Swim only where locals say conditions are safer.
Launch journeys from Dhaka can be part of the fun — carry motion comfort medicine if needed.
safety: Watch sea currents and never swim alone after dark. Keep valuables secure on crowded holiday evenings.

shortDescription: World's longest natural sea beach — Laboni evenings, Himchari views, and Inani coral stones.
overview: Cox's Bazar is Bangladesh's most visited coastal destination, known for the unbroken sandy shoreline stretching toward Teknaf. Most first-time travelers base near Laboni or Kolatoli for easy beach access and food options.
A classic short trip covers beach sunsets, Himchari viewpoint, and Inani Beach. Saint Martin's Island is a popular add-on but needs separate ship tickets and an extra day or two.
Prices rise sharply in peak winter holidays, so book hotels early if you travel in December–January.

whatToSee.title: Laboni & Kolatoli Beach
whatToSee.description: Main tourist beach stretch for walking, sunsets, and seafood dinners.

whatToSee.title: Himchari
whatToSee.description: Hill viewpoint and seasonal waterfall a short ride south of town.

whatToSee.title: Inani Beach
whatToSee.description: Coral stones and open shoreline along Marine Drive.

whatToSee.title: Marine Drive
whatToSee.description: Scenic coastal road toward Teknaf with multiple photo stops.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a direct AC bus to Cox's Bazar (about 9–11 hours). One-way AC bus tickets commonly cost around ৳1,200–৳1,800.
Flights Dhaka–Cox's Bazar take about 1 hour; fares vary widely by date (often roughly ৳4,000–৳9,000 one way in normal seasons).
From Chittagong, buses to Cox's Bazar usually take 4–5 hours.
In town, use CNG or reserved car for Himchari–Inani loops (a half-day reserved CNG often falls around ৳1,500–৳2,500 depending on negotiation and waiting time).
whereToStay: Budget guesthouses near Laboni can start near ৳1,500–৳2,500. Mid-range hotels commonly cost ৳3,500–৳7,000. Beachfront or premium properties may exceed ৳8,000–৳15,000 in peak season.
whereToEat: Beach Road and Kolatoli have many seafood restaurants. Fixed rice meals are cheaper; grilled lobster and large seafood platters cost more. Confirm prices before ordering.
foodToCarry: Snacks for Marine Drive day trips
tips: Book hotels early for Friday–Saturday peaks.
Agree CNG fares before the Himchari–Inani trip.
Carry sunscreen, hat, and sunglasses.
Keep a buffer day if you plan Saint Martin afterward.
safety: Swim in safer areas only. Watch belongings on crowded beach evenings and use licensed hotels.

shortDescription: Bangladesh's only coral island — ship from Teknaf, clear water, and quiet overnight stays.
overview: Saint Martin's Island is Bangladesh's only coral island, reached by ship from Teknaf. Most visitors overnight on the island because return ships usually leave the next day.

The charm is simple: beach walks, Chera Dwip at low tide, seafood dinners, and quieter nights than mainland Cox's Bazar. Sea conditions can cancel trips — always confirm ship schedules the day before.
Do not collect coral or harm marine life; fines and long-term damage are real issues.

whatToSee.title: Coral beaches
whatToSee.description: Shallow clear water and coral shoreline — look, do not collect.

whatToSee.title: Chera Dwip
whatToSee.description: A beautiful low-tide stretch connected at certain hours.

whatToSee.title: Sunrise points
whatToSee.description: Open eastern shorelines for early morning light.

whatToSee.title: Island cycling
whatToSee.description: Rent a bicycle (when available) to circle quieter corners of the island.

howToGo: Reach Teknaf from Dhaka/Cox's Bazar by bus. Dhaka–Teknaf is a long road day; many travelers break at Cox's Bazar.
Buy ship tickets Teknaf ↔ Saint Martin in advance in peak season. Round-trip ship tickets commonly cost around ৳1,500–৳2,500+ per person depending on operator and class.
Ships usually leave Teknaf in the morning; keep buffer time for ticket counters and boarding.
On the island, walk or use local vans/bikes for short moves between jetty, hotel, and Chera Dwip trail.
whereToStay: Cottages and hotels near the jetty area are convenient for arrivals. Simpler rooms may start near ৳2,000–৳3,500; better cottages often cost ৳4,000–৳8,000. Peak December weekends sell out quickly.
whereToEat: Hotels and beach restaurants serve seafood thalis and grilled fish. Island prices are higher than mainland. Carry snacks for ship delays.
tips: Check weather — rough seas cancel trips.
Carry cash; ATMs are limited.
Never take coral home.
Book return ship awareness into your Cox's Bazar hotel plan.
safety: Follow ship crew instructions, use life jackets when required, and swim carefully around rocks and coral.

shortDescription: World's largest mangrove forest — boat nights, deer, birds, and the Royal Bengal Tiger habitat.
overview: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO-listed treasure of Bangladesh. Most visitors join an overnight boat package from Khulna or Mongla with meals, permits, and a guide included.
Tiger sightings are uncommon. Come for the creeks, watchtowers, deer, birds, and the feeling of moving through a protected wilderness by boat.
Always use authorized operators — forest entry without proper permits is unsafe and illegal.

whatToSee.title: Mangrove creeks
whatToSee.description: Narrow water channels where the forest feels closest.

whatToSee.title: Watchtowers (Kotka / Kochikhali area)
whatToSee.description: Elevated views for deer and forest canopy when routes allow.

whatToSee.title: Wildlife moments
whatToSee.description: Spotted deer, birds, and occasional crocodile sightings from a safe distance.

whatToSee.title: Boat nights
whatToSee.description: Sleeping on the tourist vessel under river silence.

howToGo: From Dhaka, go to Khulna by bus or train (about 7–9 hours). Bus fares commonly run around ৳800–৳1,500 depending on coach type.
Join a licensed Sundarbans boat tour from Khulna/Mongla. Popular 2N/3D packages often cost about ৳10,000–৳18,000 per person including boat stay, meals, and permits (confirm inclusions).
Overnight launch packages from Dhaka are also sold by operators; compare what is included before paying.
Carry only soft bags — cabin space is limited.
whereToStay: Most itineraries use boat cabins. If you arrive a night early, budget hotels in Khulna typically cost around ৳1,500–৳3,500.
whereToEat: Meals are usually cooked on the boat for package tourists. Carry personal snacks and ORS. Inform the operator about dietary needs before boarding.
foodToCarry: Extra drinking water if you prefer bottled only
tips: Choose operators with clear permit handling and life jackets.
Mosquito repellent is essential.
Do not expect guaranteed tiger sightings.
Follow every instruction from the forest guide.
safety: Stay on the boat or approved paths. Never wander alone in the forest, especially after dark.

shortDescription: Cloud-kissed ridgelines of the Hill Tracts — sunrise above the mist from Sajek cottages.
overview: Sajek Valley is one of Bangladesh's most loved hill destinations, known for cottage stays above a sea of clouds. The usual route is Dhaka → Khagrachari → reserved jeep (Chander Gari) to Sajek.
Nights are colder than the plains, so pack a jacket even in autumn. Mobile network can be weak — download offline maps and inform family before the jeep ride.
Respect indigenous communities; ask before photographing people or homes.

whatToSee.title: Helipad viewpoint
whatToSee.description: Popular sunrise and sunset deck above the clouds.

whatToSee.title: Konglak area
whatToSee.description: Ridgeline walks and wide valley views.

whatToSee.title: Ruilui / local paras
whatToSee.description: Hill villages — visit politely with local guidance.

whatToSee.title: Cloud sea mornings
whatToSee.description: The classic Sajek photo moment after a clear night.

howToGo: Take an overnight bus from Dhaka to Khagrachari (about 8–10 hours). Tickets often cost around ৳800–৳1,400.
From Khagrachari, reserve a Chander Gari jeep to Sajek (about 3–4 hours). A full jeep is commonly around ৳8,000–৳12,000 total — sharing with other travelers lowers per-person cost.
Start the jeep ride in daylight when possible; hill roads are winding.
Return the same way; confirm jeep pickup time with your cottage host.
whereToStay: Bamboo cottages and hill resorts in Sajek usually range from about ৳2,000–৳5,000 per night for standard rooms, with premium view cottages higher on holidays. Book before arrival in peak season.
whereToEat: Cottages and small local restaurants serve rice meals and bamboo chicken. Choices are limited compared with cities — keep expectations simple and carry snacks.
foodToCarry: Warm drink sachets if you like
tips: Carry warm clothes for night and early morning.
Share jeep seats to save money.
Charge power banks — electricity can be intermittent.
Do not litter on ridgelines.
safety: Travel hill roads in daylight when you can, use trusted jeep drivers, and follow local security guidance.

shortDescription: Nilgiri clouds, Chimbuk views, Golden Temple, and hill-tract adventure routes.
overview: Bandarban is the adventure capital of the Chittagong Hill Tracts — viewpoints like Nilgiri and Chimbuk, the Golden Temple, and deeper waterfall or lake routes when permits and weather allow.
Some remote trails need local guides and current permission checks. Build a flexible plan: keep Nilgiri/Chimbuk as core highlights and treat Boga Lake or Nafakhum as conditional add-ons.
Jeep costs add up; sharing transport with other travelers keeps budgets realistic.

whatToSee.title: Nilgiri
whatToSee.description: High viewpoint famous for cloud seas and sunsets.

whatToSee.title: Chimbuk Hill
whatToSee.description: Panoramic stop often combined with Nilgiri routes.

whatToSee.title: Buddha Dhatu Jadi (Golden Temple)
whatToSee.description: Iconic Buddhist temple near Bandarban town.

whatToSee.title: Optional waterfall / lake routes
whatToSee.description: Nafakhum, Amiakhum, or Boga Lake — only with updated local advice and permits.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a direct bus to Bandarban (about 10–12 hours) or go via Chittagong. Bus fares commonly fall around ৳900–৳1,600.
In Bandarban town, hire a reserved jeep for Nilgiri/Chimbuk day trips. A jeep for popular viewpoint loops often costs roughly ৳4,000–৳8,000 total depending on stops and waiting.
For remote treks, hire licensed local guides and confirm permit rules the day before.
Keep evenings free after long jeep days — hill roads are tiring.
whereToStay: Hotels in Bandarban Sadar often cost about ৳1,500–৳4,000. Nilgiri-area cottages/resorts are higher and should be booked early, often ৳4,000–৳10,000+ in busy periods.
whereToEat: Town restaurants serve Bengali meals and some hill-tract dishes. On jeep days, carry snacks because viewpoint stalls can be limited or pricey.
foodToCarry: Packed lunch for long jeep days
tips: Confirm which areas need permits before traveling.
Share jeep costs with other travelers.
Pack rain jacket and trekking shoes.
Avoid monsoon for risky waterfall treks.
safety: Do not enter restricted zones without permission. Trek remote routes only with local guides.

shortDescription: Tea capital of Bangladesh — estate walks, seven-layer tea, and Lawachara rainforest trails.
overview: Srimangal in Moulvibazar is Bangladesh's tea capital — rolling green estates, pineapple orchards, and easy access to Lawachara National Park.
It is one of the most comfortable nature weekends from Dhaka: train or bus in, CNG sightseeing locally, and calm resort nights among tea gardens.
Seven-layer tea is a fun stop, but the real highlight is slow mornings in the estates and a guided forest walk.

whatToSee.title: Tea estates
whatToSee.description: Walk estate roads for classic Srimangal landscapes.

whatToSee.title: Lawachara National Park
whatToSee.description: Rainforest trails and birdlife with a nature guide.

whatToSee.title: Madhabpur Lake
whatToSee.description: A scenic lake stop often paired with estate visits.

whatToSee.title: Nilkantha Tea Cabin area
whatToSee.description: Famous for multi-layer tea tastings.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a train to Srimangal (scenic and popular) or a bus (about 4–5 hours). Bus/train costs commonly fall around ৳400–৳900 depending on class.
After arrival, hire a CNG for a half-day or full-day sightseeing circuit. A full-day CNG often costs roughly ৳1,500–৳2,500.
For Lawachara, go early morning and enter with a guide.
Keep one buffer evening for tea estate photography light.
whereToStay: Town hotels may start near ৳1,200–৳2,500. Tea-estate resorts commonly cost about ৳3,000–৳7,000 depending on season and facilities.
whereToEat: Local restaurants serve Sylheti meals; resorts include breakfast more often than full board. Try pineapple in season from local vendors.
tips: Morning light is best in tea gardens.
Hire a guide inside Lawachara.
Weekdays are quieter than weekends.
Carry leech socks/repellent in wet months.
safety: Stay on marked forest trails and do not feed wildlife.

shortDescription: Freshwater swamp forest near Sylhet — boat under a green canopy when water levels rise.
bestTime: June – September (high water); also visitable in winter
overview: Ratargul is Bangladesh's best-known freshwater swamp forest, reached by a short trip from Sylhet city and a wooden boat ride under trees.
Monsoon and post-rain months give the classic flooded-forest look. In drier months the experience changes with water level — still beautiful, but different.
Go early to avoid crowds and agree the boat fare before boarding.

whatToSee.title: Boat trails under trees
whatToSee.description: The signature Ratargul route through flooded forest corridors.

whatToSee.title: Birdlife
whatToSee.description: Quiet watching from the boat, especially in calmer hours.

whatToSee.title: Seasonal flooded forest
whatToSee.description: Water level transforms the scenery — ask locals about current conditions.

howToGo: Reach Sylhet from Dhaka by bus (about 5–6 hours) or flight (about 1 hour). Buses often cost around ৳600–৳1,000; flights vary by date.
From Sylhet, hire a CNG to Goainghat / Ratargul area (about 1 hour). Round CNG hire commonly costs around ৳1,500–৳2,500 depending on waiting.
At the ghat, hire a local boat into the swamp forest. Boat fares vary by group size and route — confirm before boarding.
Combine with Jaflong/Bisanakandi only if you start very early.
whereToStay: Base in Sylhet city hotels (often ৳1,500–৳4,000). Day-tripping is the normal approach; overnight options near the forest are limited.
whereToEat: Eat in Sylhet city before/after. Carry snacks for the boat because options at the entry point are basic.
tips: Ask about water level before you go.
Protect cameras from splash.
Avoid peak holiday midday crowds.
Do not stand suddenly in small boats.
safety: Sit steadily, use life jackets when provided, and avoid boats in bad weather.

shortDescription: Stone-river landscapes under the Meghalaya hills — classic Sylhet day-trip pair.
bestTime: October – March (also dramatic in green monsoon months)
overview: Jaflong and Bisanakandi are the classic nature day trips from Sylhet city — rivers, stones, and the green wall of the Meghalaya hills across the border landscape.
Most travelers hire one CNG/microbus and cover both in a single long day. Start early, especially if you also want Ratargul.
Monsoon makes scenes lusher but paths more slippery; winter is easier for walking and photos.

whatToSee.title: Piyain River (Jaflong)
whatToSee.description: Open river views with hill backdrop — Jaflong's main draw.

whatToSee.title: Bisanakandi stone river
whatToSee.description: Photogenic water and stone landscapes toward Companyganj.

whatToSee.title: Hill border scenery
whatToSee.description: Green slopes that define Sylhet's tourism identity.

howToGo: Base in Sylhet city after arriving from Dhaka by bus or flight.
Hire a CNG or microbus for a Jaflong + Bisanakandi circuit. A full-day reserved CNG commonly costs around ৳2,000–৳3,500.
Keep 30–45 minutes between spots for traffic and photo stops.
If combining Ratargul, do swamp forest first in the morning and hills afterward only with a disciplined schedule.
whereToStay: Stay in Sylhet city (৳1,500–৳4,000 typical mid budget). Same-day return is standard.
whereToEat: Local restaurants near tourist points serve basic meals; many travelers eat a proper lunch back in Sylhet. Carry water in the vehicle.
tips: Start by 7–8 AM.
Wear shoes with grip in wet months.
Agree the full CNG route and fare before leaving the hotel.
Keep passport advice in mind only if instructed near sensitive border zones.
safety: Stay away from strong river currents and follow local guidance near border-adjacent viewpoints.

shortDescription: Lake district of the Hill Tracts — hanging bridge, boat days, and shoreline hills.
overview: Rangamati is known for Kaptai Lake, the hanging bridge, and a softer hill-tracts experience than hard trekking routes in Bandarban.
A full-day boat on the lake is the heart of the trip. Pair it with the Tribal Cultural Institute and lakeside evenings in town.
Negotiate boat packages clearly — hours, stops, and fuel should be agreed before leaving the ghat.

whatToSee.title: Kaptai Lake
whatToSee.description: Wide lake waters and green hill shores by boat.

whatToSee.title: Hanging Bridge
whatToSee.description: Rangamati's iconic photo stop (expect crowds on holidays).

whatToSee.title: Shuvolong
whatToSee.description: Waterfall stop when water levels allow on boat routes.

whatToSee.title: Tribal Cultural Institute
whatToSee.description: A useful cultural context stop in town.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a bus to Rangamati (often via Chittagong). Expect a long road day; fares commonly around ৳900–৳1,600.
In Rangamati, walk or use local transport to the hanging bridge and ghat areas.
Hire a lake boat for a half-day or full-day circuit. Full-day boats for a small group often cost roughly ৳3,000–৳6,000 total depending on route and season.
Return to town before dark unless your operator plans a specific evening schedule.
whereToStay: Hotels near Reserve Bazar / town usually range about ৳1,500–৳4,500. Lakeside resorts cost more when available.
whereToEat: Town restaurants serve lake fish and Bengali meals. Carry snacks on long boat days.
tips: Ask for life jackets on the boat.
Confirm Shuvolong feasibility the same day.
Weekends are busier at the hanging bridge.
Respect local hill communities.
safety: Wear life jackets, avoid overloaded boats, and follow the boatman's weather calls.

shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist monastery ruins — ancient Bengal's architectural grandeur.
overview: Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of South Asia's most important early medieval Buddhist monastery ruins.
Pair it with Mahasthangarh near Bogura for a strong north-west heritage weekend from Dhaka. Hire a local guide at the site for historical context.
This is a walking and learning trip more than an adventure trek — bring a hat and water for open courtyard sun.

whatToSee.title: Somapura Mahavihara complex
whatToSee.description: The vast cruciform monastery ruins and surrounding cells.

whatToSee.title: Site museum
whatToSee.description: Artifacts and explanations that make the ruins easier to understand.

whatToSee.title: Mahasthangarh (combo)
whatToSee.description: Ancient citadel near Bogura — excellent same-circuit partner.

howToGo: From Dhaka, take a bus toward Jaipurhat / Naogaon / Bogura (about 5–7 hours depending on route). Fares often around ৳500–৳900.
Use local CNG/auto from the nearest town to the Paharpur site.
If combining Mahasthangarh, base one night in Bogura and split sites across two half-days.
Start morning visits to avoid heat and harsh midday light.
whereToStay: Hotels in Bogura or Jaipurhat/Naogaon typically cost about ৳1,200–৳3,500 for standard rooms. Many travelers use Bogura as the more convenient base.
whereToEat: Eat in town before/after site visits. On-site food options are limited — carry water and snacks.
tips: Hire a guide for history context.
Wear comfortable walking shoes.
Do not climb restricted walls.
Combine with Mahasthangarh for better value.
safety: Watch your step on uneven brick ruins and keep hydrated in open sun.

shortDescription: Mughal forts, Ahsan Manzil, lane life, and legendary food walks in historic Dhaka.
overview: Old Dhaka packs centuries of history into narrow lanes: Lalbagh Fort, Ahsan Manzil, historic mosques, riverfront glimpses at Sadarghat, and some of the city's most famous food.
It is best done on foot with a local guide or a planned map route. Fridays and public holidays can change monument hours — check before you go.
Keep your bag light and your phone secure in crowded bazaars.

whatToSee.title: Ahsan Manzil
whatToSee.description: The Pink Palace museum on the riverfront side of old town history.

whatToSee.title: Lalbagh Fort
whatToSee.description: Mughal fort complex and one of Dhaka's essential heritage stops.

whatToSee.title: Chawk Bazar lanes
whatToSee.description: Dense market life, traditional foods, and old-city atmosphere.

whatToSee.title: Sadarghat riverfront
whatToSee.description: Buriganga boat traffic and classic Dhaka river scenes.

howToGo: From anywhere in Dhaka, use ride-sharing, CNG, or bus toward Lalbagh / Islampur / Sadarghat areas.
Do the core loop on foot between nearby monuments to avoid traffic loops.
Use rickshaw only for short hops when lanes allow.
Start morning to finish key indoor sites before afternoon heat and crowds.
whereToStay: Stay in central Dhaka neighborhoods (Motijheel side, Gulshan/Banani/Dhanmondi for comfort) and day-visit Old Dhaka. Old-town lodging is less common for first-time visitors.
whereToEat: This is a food destination: bakarkhani, kebabs, biryani, and sweets. Choose busy, popular shops and carry hand sanitizer.
tips: Go with a companion in the busiest lanes.
Keep phones and wallets secure.
Check monument opening days.
Eat where turnover is high.
safety: Mind pickpockets in crowds and use trusted transport after dark.

shortDescription: Vast wetland horizon of Sunamganj — boat nights, birds, and monsoon water-country silence.
bestTime: June – September for high water; winter for birds
overview: Tanguar Haor in Sunamganj feels like an inland sea in monsoon — open water, sky, and stilt-like village edges. In winter, birdlife becomes a major draw.
The usual plan is Dhaka → Sunamganj → Tahirpur ghat → engine boat with overnight on board. Network signals can drop, so share your plan before boarding.
Choose operators who provide life jackets and clear meal inclusions.

whatToSee.title: Open haor horizon
whatToSee.description: Endless water-and-sky views, especially in high-water months.

whatToSee.title: Migratory birds (seasonal)
whatToSee.description: Winter birdwatching is a highlight for many travelers.

whatToSee.title: Haor villages
whatToSee.description: Waterside communities and a completely different rhythm from city life.

whatToSee.title: Boat sunrise
whatToSee.description: Quiet morning light from the deck.

howToGo: Take a bus from Dhaka to Sunamganj (about 6–8 hours). Fares commonly around ৳700–৳1,200.
From Sunamganj, continue to Tahirpur / boat ghat by local transport.
Hire an engine boat package for overnight haor cruising. Per-person package costs often land around ৳5,000–৳10,000+ depending on group size, boat quality, and meals.
Return via the same route; keep a flexible buffer for weather.
whereToStay: Overnight on the tourist boat is the core experience. If needed, basic lodges in Sunamganj/Tahirpur may cost roughly ৳1,000–৳2,500.
whereToEat: Boat packages usually include simple rice meals and haor fish. Carry backup dry food in case of delays.
foodToCarry: Water purifying tablets or extra bottled water
tips: Monsoon = high water drama; winter = birds.
Waterproof your phone and clothes.
Confirm life jackets before payment.
Inform family about weak network zones.
safety: Weather changes fast on open water. Use life jackets and never travel through storms.

shortDescription: High Bandarban viewpoint above the clouds — short premium hill escape for sunrise and sunset.
overview: Nilgiri is one of Bandarban's most famous viewpoints — a place travelers visit for sunset color and, on clear mornings, a sea of clouds below the hills.
Most people reach Nilgiri by jeep from Bandarban Sadar. Fog can block views, so winter clear mornings are the safest bet for the classic panorama.
Follow all local area rules; this is a managed hill station zone.

whatToSee.title: Cloud sea viewpoint

whatToSee.description: A common jeep-stop panorama paired with Nilgiri trips.

howToGo: First reach Bandarban town from Dhaka/Chittagong by bus.
Hire a reserved jeep to Nilgiri (about 1.5–2 hours). Round-trip jeep hire commonly costs around ৳3,500–৳6,000 depending on waiting time and season.
If staying overnight at Nilgiri cottages, book before travel and confirm entry/ticket rules.
Carry a warm layer — evenings are colder than Bandarban town.
whereToStay: Nilgiri cottages/resorts should be booked early; nights often cost about ৳4,000–৳10,000+ in busy periods. Budget travelers day-trip from Bandarban town hotels (৳1,500–৳4,000).
whereToEat: Resort restaurants cover most overnight guest meals. Day-trippers should eat in Bandarban town and carry snacks for the viewpoint.
tips: Clear winter mornings beat foggy evenings for clouds.
Book cottages before arriving.
Respect photography restrictions if posted.
Combine with Chimbuk to maximize the jeep day.
safety: Follow site rules, stay behind barriers at cliff edges, and avoid unnecessary night movement on hill roads.
